finding.claim: POST /profile/avatar fetches an attacker-supplied URL server-side. The only check is a case-sensitive startsWith('https://') prefix test, so internal HTTPS hosts are reachable directly, and redirects to internal plain-HTTP targets (e.g. 169.254.169.254 or users.internal:8080) bypass the scheme check. Only the response body length is returned, so this is a blind, GET-only SSRF with a size oracle.

trace.note: avatarUrl read from request body with no normalization
typeof string and url.startsWith('https://') prefix check only; no URL parsing, host/IP allowlist, or private-address block
axios.get fetches the unchanged URL; axios follows redirects by default in Node; no timeout or maxContentLength
res.json returns img.data.length, a response-size oracle to the caller

finding.guards_checked: Type check and https:// prefix check at server.js:11 only. Not present: URL parsing, hostname/IP allowlist, private/loopback/link-local/metadata block, DNS-rebinding defense, port restriction, redirect disabling or per-hop revalidation, timeout, size limit, authentication on the route. No package.json or lockfile in the directory, so the axios version and its redirect defaults were not verified by running code.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only check is server.js:11 (typeof string plus a case-sensitive startsWith("https://") prefix). Nothing else in server.js validates the URL before the sink at server.js:14: no URL parsing, host or IP allowlist, private-address block, redirect restriction, timeout, or size limit. The route at server.js:9 has no authentication, and app.use(express.json()) at server.js:5 is only a body parser.
verdict.reason: The attacker-controlled value req.body.avatarUrl (server.js:10) reaches axios.get (server.js:14) and the only check is the prefix test at server.js:11, which does not stop internal https hosts or redirects; the response length is returned at server.js:15. Caveat: the redirect-to-HTTP path depends on axios's default redirect following in Node, which can't be confirmed here because there is no package.json or lockfile. The direct internal-HTTPS SSRF does not depend on that.
